newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EMS-Chemie offers to buy back more shares.
newsitem.headline: EMS-Chemie offers to buy back more shares.

text.p: Swiss chemicals group Ems-Chemie Holding AG, which bought shares in March rather than paying a dividend, said it was now offering to buy a further 14,140 bearer shares at 6,100 Swiss francs per share.
Ems-Chemie bearer shares closed on the Swiss bourse at 6,125 Swiss francs shortly before the announcement, off a high of 6,170 from April 30.
The holding company for the Ems Group said it was making the additional offer based on good result at the holding, which closed its 1996/97 financial year on April 30.
The holding's net profit jumped to 317 million Swiss francs from 166 million in 1995/96, the statement said.

"The extraordinary increase in profit resulted from higher securities earnings of 288 million Swiss francs (year before: 161 million) and higher earnings from participations of 55 million (year before: 19 million)," the statement said.
Ems-Chemie said it would publish details of the latest buy-back offer on May 9 or May 10.
The company in March bought back 40,000 shares at 6,000 Swiss francs each after saying it preferred the offer to paying a dividend on 1996/97 results.
The EMS Group, whose 1996 year closed on December 31, reported on February 28 that last year's net profit rose 12.2 percent to 229 million Swiss francs.
The latest offer would raise the number bought back to 54,140 or 9.02 percent of cpaital for a toatl of 326 million Swiss francs, the statement said.
Share capital would be reduced from 30 million Swiss francs to 27.293 million.
